newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian reporters freed in Chechnya after 3 months.
newsitem.headline: Russian reporters freed in Chechnya after 3 months.

text.p: Four Russian journalists were freed on Friday after more than three months of captivity in separatist Chechnya and President Boris Yeltsin praised Chechen leader Aslan Maskhadov for his role in their release.
Three others, a television crew from the NTV commercial station, are still being held in the breakaway region.
"Maskhadov and many federal officials have worked persistently for this. They found them and freed them, they did not abandon them," Yeltsin told reporters at the start of a visit to St Petersburg.
Three of the journalists are from Radio Russia and the fourth, Nikolai Zagnoiko, works for Itar-Tass news agency. "All four are alive and in good health," Zagnoiko told Tass.
Yeltsin called for joint action by Russia and Chechnya to fight terrorism. "If anything happens, we never back down," he said. "Fighting terrorism is one of the main presidential programmes."
Chechnya's towns and cities were ruined in 21 months of fighting between separatists and Russian troops trying to quell an independence drive.

Nearly every man has a weapon and jobs are scarce. Fighting ended last August after tens of thousands of people were killed and peace was sealed in a deal signed in Moscow last month by Yeltsin and Maskhadov.
The freeing of hostages, especially Russian journalists, has become a burning issue for Maskhadov who, surrounded by powerful field commanders, has to prove his grip on power.
Interfax new agency quoted Russia's Security Council Secretary, Ivan Rybkin, as praising Maskhadov's efforts.
"Maskhadov's success will bolster his influence among his voters," Rybkin said.
"But not everyone in Grozny and Moscow will clap their hands," he added in a clear reference to so-called "parties of war" on both sides which want fighting to continue.
Rybkin said the freeing of the journalists would help the development of the peace process in Chechnya. A Chechen delegation is in Moscow for talks on economic issues.
Chechen and Russian officials said the journalists had been freed without ransom and were on the way home.

A Chechen police and commando raid last week freed six hostages, including an Austrian businessman. Maskhkadov, who has pledged to fight the wave of kidnapping, has said such operations would be held often.
